newsitem.title: THAILAND: Big Thai note issue won't hit liquidity - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Big Thai note issue won't hit liquidity - dealers.

text.p: Liquidity in the Thai money market is unlikely to be affected by the massive 20-billion-baht issue of 28-day notes on Friday, dealers said.

The financial system would continue to be flush with funds when a substantial amount of money is expected to enter the market from newly launched state pension funds later this month, they told Reuters.

"The impact from the big bill auction will be minimal because the increased amount of bonds auctioned is very small compared with the amount of state funds due to enter the system," said one dealer at an American bank.
The Bank of Thailand raised its 28-day bill auction to 20 billion baht from 2.0 billion originally planned on Friday. The average yield was 10.38 percent for the bills.

The central bank said it had substantially raised the amount of bonds auctioned to mop up excess liquidity in the system after a scheduled withdrawal of about 70-80 billion baht of start-up funds by the Government Pension Fund on March 27.
Olarn Chaiprawat, president of Siam Commercial Bank Plc, said earlier this week he expected the funds entering the system from the state pension funds to weigh on interest rates.
Current high liquidity was also the result of a heavy inflow of foreign funds, reflecting sliding swap premiums, dealers said.
"The swap premium has been falling sharply this week. There was heavy selling of the forward dollar," another senior dealer at a local bank said.
At 0324 GMT, the baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 7.50/8.50 satangs per dollar compared with 8.00/9.00 in early morning.
The swap premium moved around 11.00/12.00 satangs late last week.
